context.description: The session watch and the hooks hold no state of their own

evidence.trustReason: Given the session watch and hook modules after phase 2: the test parses core/sessions.ts and core/hooks.ts whole, plus the sessionEvents actor of core/workers.ts with its helpers (toolEvents, statusEvent, of, TurnEvent), and asserts all five declarations were extracted. When they are inspected / Then no Ref, no MutableHashMap and no polled loop: a TypeScript-AST scan for Ref-family and MutableHashMap-family imports and uses, new Map/Set, endless and sleeping loops, Effect.repeat/forever/schedule, Schedule.*, Stream.tick, setInterval/setTimeout, module-level let/var and classes returns []; a negative control over a planted source proves the scan finds every one of those constructs. The module exports are read from the real modules: no builderTurn in TaskSessions, no ready/verdicts/repeated/limits/watch/unwatch/take* in TaskHooks, every member a function, string or non-global RegExp. My own grep of sessions.ts and hooks.ts agrees. And stall, idle and the spend cap are delayed transitions and guards of the task supervisor: the real TaskSupervisor node tree shows watching has one 'after streamIdle' -> stalling (none in the tool state), turn.status has the spendCap guard in watching and tool, and the ended state's always rows are capped, repeated, readied, nudgeLeft, else unready, each guard and the delay a machine implementation. Live on a SimulatedClock: 3 s of wall time records nothing, 1990 ms records nothing, 2000 ms records task.stalled; with the clock still, an idle end records task.nudged 1 and a spend-cap retry records task.needs_human. Fresh run: 6 pass, 0 fail, 80 expect calls.
